title: streaming-sse-chunking-backpressure-debug-notes-lucas
content:
Context:
- Investigating intermittent client-side delays when consuming streaming SSE responses from the hosted inference endpoint. Some clients (browser EventSource / fetch readable stream) see messages only after the model finishes or after large pauses, rather than receiving steady token-level updates.
- Repro is easier when the model response is long (>1k tokens) and client is intentionally slow/paused to simulate backpressure.
- Suspect interactions between our runtime chunking, proxy buffering (nginx/ELB), and client read patterns.

Observed behavior summary:
- In 60% of repro runs, client receives a burst of data only when the server completes or after a long pause (10s+).
- In ~30% of runs, small chunks arrive as expected (token-by-token).
- Logs on server side show writes happening continuously (write latency ~1-5ms), but bytes_sent from proxy show large aggregated writes.
- Repro across environments: local server -> client works fine. Behind nginx (staging) shows delayed delivery. Behind ALB also shows buffering in some cases.

Quick hypothesis list:
- Proxy (nginx/ALB) buffer/flush behavior is coalescing chunks when client is slow. Need to ensure no proxy buffering (proxy_buffering off) and that we use chunked transfer encoding with proper flushes.
- Our runtime's token buffering: maybe we batch tokens into larger frames before writing to socket (configurable batch window). But server logs indicate small writes are happening, so likely not the primary cause.
- TLS/connection-level Nagle-like aggregation? TCP_NODELAY might be disabled somewhere, causing aggregation.
- Express/compression or middleware adding Content-Length or buffering; need to disable compression for SSE endpoints.
- Client read code: fetch() with ReadableStream reader requires manual read() loop — if implemented wrong, could block until stream closed. But EventSource should receive incremental messages. Different clients show different failure rates.

Commands / repro steps I ran:
1) Minimal curl test (no proxy, local server):
   # start local server (node/server.js - simple SSE that writes every 100ms)
   curl -N http://localhost:3000/sse
   # -N to disable buffering in curl

   Observed: token-like lines streamed continuously. Good.

2) Curl against staging (behind nginx):
   curl -N -v https://staging.redwood-inference.internal/sse-test
   # Verbose shows: HTTP/2 200; chunked transfer encoding; but body arrives in large lumps

   Snippet from curl verbose (timings, sizes):
   * Received 16384 bytes chunk after 00.10s pause
   * No visible 100ms incremental events

3) Using httpie (stream mode):
   http --stream GET https://staging.redwood-inference.internal/sse-test
   # Similar to curl: intermittent bursts, not steady stream

4) Node repro client variations:
   // node-fetch reader (slow consumer emulation)
   const res = await fetch(url);
   const reader = res.body.getReader();
   while(true) { const {done, value} = await reader.read(); if(done) break; await sleep(200); // artificially slow consumer
   console.log('got', value.length); }
   Observed: often reader.read() returns big concatenated buffers instead of many small ones.

5) Bypassed nginx with tcpdump on server to verify bytes leaving server socket in small writes:
   # tcpdump -i eth0 -s 0 -w out.pcap tcp port 443
   -> confirms server is sending small frames at 100ms intervals. So server writes are small and timely.

6) Nginx config tests:
   - Added proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; chunked_transfer_encoding on; proxy_set_header Connection ""; proxy_buffer_size 4k
   - After toggling proxy_buffering off, behavior improved dramatically (steady small chunks).
   - When proxy_buffering on (default), chunks coalesced.

7) ALB (AWS LB) behavior:
   - ALB seems to not buffer for plain HTTP/1.1 streaming, but if HTTP/2 is used between ALB and backend it may re-chunk.
   - Repro: forced HTTP/1.1 upstream and it improved.

8) Additional checks:
   - Verified response headers from server: Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8; Cache-Control: no-cache; Connection: keep-alive
   - Ensured we are not sending Content-Length. Confirmed Transfer-Encoding: chunked is present.
   - Added res.flush() (node) after every write; in some environments flush is no-op unless compression disabled.

Errors and logs observed:
- Proxy error log (nginx): "upstream sent too big header" in unrelated runs (might be separate)
- Client-side console (browser): no explicit errors, just long pauses
- Server app logs show no exceptions; runtime shows small write latencies

Actionable next steps (short term):
- For staging: keep proxy_buffering off for SSE endpoints and add explicit config in nginx upstream blocks. Document in infra repo.
- Add a health/test endpoint that streams synthetic tokens for QA on customer infra to detect buffering behavior.
- Ensure our hosted API uses HTTP/1.1 for upstream to avoid HTTP/2 re-chunking issues, or validate ALB/nginx settings for HTTP/2->1.1 translation.
- Add telemetry: measure per-request time between first byte and subsequent bytes, and percent of requests that deliver first token within X ms. Surface in Console traces.
- Client SDKs: add guidance for using EventSource or fetch with proper ReadableStream handling, and a checkbox to detect server buffering.

Longer term hypotheses to test:
- Some cloud proxies will always re-chunk for small writes to optimize network; may need to increase our minimum chunk size for those paths (tradeoff: latency vs chunking reliability).
- Evaluate adding periodic no-op SSE comments (":\n") or keepalive every < itv > to nudge proxies to flush. This is a common pattern.

Quick repro commands to share with infra team:
- Curl (staging, shows buffering):
  curl -N -v https://staging.redwood-inference.internal/sse-test
- Curl bypassing nginx (direct to instance private IP):
  curl -N -v http://10.0.3.45:3000/sse-test
- Minimal node server (run locally to reproduce good behavior):
  // node/server-sse.js
  const http = require('http');
  http.createServer((req, res) => {
    res.writeHead(200, {'Content-Type':'text/event-stream','Cache-Control':'no-cache','Connection':'keep-alive'});
    let i=0;
    const t = setInterval(() => { res.write(`data: token-${i}\n\n`); i++; if(i>100) { clearInterval(t); res.end(); } }, 100);
  }).listen(3000);
  curl -N http://localhost:3000/

- Test script for slow client (node):
  // client-slow.js
  const fetch = require('node-fetch');
  (async ()=>{ const r = await fetch(process.argv[2]); const reader = r.body.getReader(); for(;;){ const {done, value} = await reader.read(); if(done) break; console.log('chunk len', value.length); await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,200)); } })()

Notes / breadcrumbs for infra PR:
- nginx: ensure upstream block for /sse endpoints has:
    proxy_buffering off;
    proxy_http_version 1.1;
    chunked_transfer_encoding on;
    proxy_set_header Connection "";
- ALB: prefer HTTP/1.1 to backend where possible if we need token-level delivery guarantees; test with and without HTTP/2.
- CDN/edge/ingress rules: verify they don't apply response buffering for SSE endpoints.

Open questions:
- Do we want to document/ship a server-side minimal buffering guarantee (e.g., min-chunk-size) to handle noisy proxies?
- Should SDK detect large initial delays and surface a warning to customers (probable mis-configuration on their infra)?

TL;DR:
- Server is writing small chunks correctly. Proxy buffering (nginx/ALB) + HTTP/2 multiplexing is the most likely cause. Turning proxy_buffering off on staging fixed the issue. Next steps: infra config, telemetry, and SDK guidance.

Random notes to self:
- Check if envoy sidecars have tcp_buffer_limit or http_response_buffer limits.
- Add a small test to our e2e infra tests that asserts token-level delivery for a long-running stream (should fail in default nginx config).
- Follow up with networking team re: TLS-level aggregation (SACK/TCP_NODELAY) - but lower priority.

End of notes.
